Event Swatch

Motion·by @artntek·2026-08-26·inspora page·original post

What it is

Calendar drag physics: dragging an event chip in a week view lifts it with a playful tilt and stretch - the chip rotates with drag velocity, shows a floating time pill ('Wed 8:00 AM'), dims/blurs the remaining events, and rubber-bands on drop; multiple selected chips stack and fan like cards in hand.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-20%
Week grid (Wed 26 - Sat 29) with colorful event chips (yellow, green, purple, pink, orange, blue); hover lifts one chip slightly with shadow.
20-40%
Drag: grabbed chip scales ~1.05, rotates a few degrees matching cursor velocity, casts a large soft shadow; a dark time pill ('Wed 8:00 AM') floats above it; background events fade to ~50%.
40-60%
Chip travels across day columns; target slot shows a ghost outline; chip tilts opposite when direction reverses; nearby chips shift aside.
60-85%
Multi-select drag: 3-4 chips stack with slight rotational fan (-6deg..+6deg) like held cards, time pill on top; they swing as a group with lag.
85-100%
Drop: chip springs into the slot (small overshoot + squash), background restores, pill fades; single blue chip dropped alone in an empty day.

Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: calendar drag physics - dragging an event chip in a week view lifts it with a playful tilt and stretch: the chip rotates with drag velocity, shows a floating time pill ("Wed 8:00 AM"), dims the remaining events, and rubber-bands on drop. Multi-selected chips stack and fan like cards in hand.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Week grid (Wed 26 - Sat 29) with colorful event chips (yellow, green, purple, pink, orange, blue). A dark time pill floats above the dragged chip. Drop targets show as ghost outlines in day columns.

## Motion spec
Pattern: gesture drag with physics flavor.
- Hover: chip lifts slightly with a small shadow (120ms).
- Grab: chip scales 1 -> 1.05 over 150ms, casts a large soft shadow; background events fade to ~50% opacity (200ms).
- Drag: chip trails the cursor with spring lag (stiffness ~300, damping ~22); rotation proportional to cursor x-velocity (a few degrees, tilting opposite on direction reversals); time pill rides above, updating as the chip crosses slots; target slot shows a ghost outline; nearby chips shift aside with layout animation.
- Multi-select: 3-4 chips stack with a rotational fan (-6deg..+6deg) like held cards, swinging as a group with shared lag.
- Drop: chip springs into the slot (small overshoot + squash, ~400ms); background restores; pill fades (150ms).

## Calibration
- The cursor lag (300/22 spring) is the personality - chips should feel held, not glued.
- Rotation comes from velocity per frame, never a fixed tilt.
- Drop overshoot is small (2-3%) with a squash; a big bounce reads as a game.

## Reduced motion
Chips move 1:1 with the cursor (no lag/rotation); drop snaps with a 150ms fade; no fan on multi-drag.

## Don't miss
- Background dimming (~50%) focuses the drag - everything else leaves the stage.
- The time pill is dark, mono, and always above the chip stack.
- Multi-drag fans by rotation around the grab point, not a flat stack offset.
